# It is known that the fundamental group of the boundary OV of the solid torus V is the free

abelian group on two generators E x 2.

Therefore one can define a longitude for V as a simple.

closed curve on OV that is of the form (k, 1) in the fundamental group of the boundary 8V, & € &.

A meridian is a simple, closed curve of the form (1,0).

Definition 3.1. Let D be a diagram of an oriented link L and let ci, o2 be two components of

D. The linking number between e and o is the total number of positive crossings minus the total number of negative crossings, divided by 2, over all crossings between e and c2. A positive crossing is when one has to rotate the over are counterclockwise, in order to align the two arcs involved, so that they both point to the same direction. A negative crossing is when the upper strand has to rotate clockwise. The linking number counts the algebraic number of times one component winds around the other one. Further, it is an ambient isotopy invariant as it respects Reidemeister Il and I moves and it is not affected by the Reidemeister I move. Thus we talk about the kaang nurber of two fink components as the linking number between them in any diagram representative of the link.

neighbourhood in S that is a solid torus S' x D2 = V, where K is the core of V. Let Ko be a

longitude in V with the same orientation as K. The linking number Ik(K, Ko) between K and Ko, is called a framing of K. For an example view Fig. 6a. A framed link of c-components is a link of whom each one of the c components is a framed knot.
